Prove or refute one NEW narrower bridge for native torsion-coordinate heights: arithmetic contraction from a cover-compatible nodal model to the relatively minimal one. This is not a retry of a broad height synthesis (that report was EMPTY). Input: degree-d cover pi:C->P1 over number field K, positive genus g, fixed total branch count r and branch LOG height hB. Reviewed analytic/Faltings bounds in context are proved. Javanpeykar normalization-resolution Z has pi morphism, semistable regular nodal fibres, not necessarily relatively minimal. Book9.2.5 proof needs relatively minimal Y, and exact negative sign is -(D,D-omega)/2. Contract rational (-1) tails f:Z->Y. A rational section b lies above integer a, and pole divisor P=pi^*(infty) on generic curve; after finite extension split into sections. On Z the b/pole sections are disjoint at finite places. Proposed elementary repair: each smooth-point blowdown increases finite intersection of b with one pole section by at most the corresponding loss h_Z(b)-h_Y(b) in normalized Arakelov height. Since minimal h_Y(b)>=0, I_Y(b,P)/[K:Q] <= d*h_Z(b), independently of extension degree and number of blowups. Is this true for split semistable regular models, all contractions including nodes, genus1, and sections through exceptional components? Prove exact intersection/adjunction identities or counterexample. If valid, extend ONLY as far as warranted to the book9.2.5 cross-intersection term with D=g b, using supplied global Green lower bound for archimedean terms. Do NOT claim full coordinate-height bound without paying the vertical pole term of book9.1.3, theta supremum, and integral model. Investigate one further sharply named term if you can: can vertical pole multiplicity on Y of pi be bounded by O(poly(d)*(1+hB)) from normalization plus resolution, or is cover/model data needed? Explicitly separate this additional conjecture. Return usable complete proof, not a whole-program essay. Strongest falsifier: nonminimal genus1 blowup violates omega^2>=0/nefness; source review supplies it. No tools, browsing, API, archives. State constants, normalization, quantifiers, source-dependent versus new deductions.

# Uniform arithmetic height: established pieces and remaining coordinate bound

2026-11-12. Native classical surface comparison remains OPEN. This note
records two proved sub-obligations from the accelerated closure round.
Paid reports remain advisory; independent proofs and actual sources were
parent-checked. No whole point-counting, novelty or quantum-separation claim.

## Stable Faltings height is now bounded uniformly

Fix r>=3. For every finite degree-d map pi:Y->P1 over Qbar with Y smooth,
projective, connected of genus g>=1 and total Galois orbit of branch points
of cardinality <=r, put hB=max h(beta), ABSOLUTE LOGARITHMIC projective height.
Then, for an effective C_r depending only on r,

    h_Fal(Y) <= C_r*d^5*(d+1+hB).

Proof and exact source ledger:
audits/reviews/2026-11-12-surface-faltings-transfer.md. It combines the proved
MERKL_LOG_COLLISION_ATLAS.md with actual Javanpeykar1403.6404 Theorem2.4.1,
Lemma2.3.1, Proposition4.2.4 and Theorem4.3.2. It does not reinterpret the
source's exponential HB as logarithmic. Field enlargement in the height
proof is existential and cancels after normalization; no algorithm for a
semistable model or its extension field is asserted.

The precise product-formula identity is
I_fin(P,Q)+sum_sigma log(1/vartheta_sigma(P,Q))=[K:Q](h(P)+h(Q)),
with vartheta using maximum homogeneous norms. Consequently both normalized
finite intersections and average log inverse chordal distance are bounded
by h(P)+h(Q)+log2. Thus average L_sigma<=1+r(r-1)(2hB+log2).

The FULL Merkl atlas gives |log||dz||_Ar|<=Lambda_sigma, not just sup gr.
The actual angular Whitney/root charts also have
|d(pi^*t)/dz|>=dist_ch(pi(x),B)/800 at finite base values. For a rational
a outside B, every b over a therefore satisfies

    hAr(b) <= Lambda_bar +(d+1)*sum_beta(h(beta)+h(a)+log2)
              +2d²logd+log800,
    Lambda_bar <= C_r*d³*(d+1+hB).

The finite term uses the general-cover normalization with vertical branch
only at primes<=d; horizontal branch collisions are explicitly charged by
the same product formula. The factorial-normalized source Wronskian has
lognorm<=g(g+1)Lambda_sigma/2+O(g²+glog(gd)) by Cauchy/Hadamard and
full-chart density<=d². Choose a among1,...,g³+r+1 avoiding branch and
Weierstrass images; g=O_r(d) and h(a)=O_r(logd). Actual Theorem2.4.1 gives
the displayed h_Fal bound, including genus one and branches at infinity.

This proves an intrinsic inequality, not model-coordinate heights or
reconstruction precision. The twist family y²=a*x(x-1)(x-2) still forces
charging supplied-model coefficients. The completed Claude faltings report
is accepted after repairing its containing-branch-set equality and Wronskian
normalization. No theorem is inferred from its verdict label.

## One common point makes canonical divisors unique

For ANY smooth projective geometrically connected genus-g curve C/k and ANY
N geometric degree-zero classes T, assume char0 or char(k)>2g-2. Outside at
most

    [0 in T]*(g³-g)+|T\{0}|*floor(g(g-1)²/2) <= N*g³

geometric points b, every E in T has h0(E(gb))=1. Hence it has a UNIQUE
effective degree-g representative D_E. This descends as a CLOSED divisor
over the field fixing b and E, without splitting geometric supports.

Independent proof: audits/reviews/2026-11-12-surface-common-basepoint.md.
RR reduces failure to a section of K tensor E^-1 vanishing to order g.
The complete-series Wronskian has local leading Vandermonde in vanishing
orders <=2g-2; it is nonzero in the stated characteristic. Total weights
are g³-g for E=0 and g(g-1)² otherwise; nonzero-class bad points consume
weight>=2. This verifies the printed portion of the PARTIAL Claude report;
unprinted growing-rank/lazy-certification assertions are not admitted.

Characteristic is a real gate: the smooth char3 plane quartic
y³z+yz³=x⁴ has genus3 and every tangent contact>=3, so h0(3b)>=2 at EVERY
b. At an affine (a,b), substitution gives (x-a^9)(a-x)³; infinity has
contact4. Thus no unrestricted-characteristic bad-set assertion survives.

For a separable plane map of degree D with discriminant exclusions R,
enumerate N*g³+R+1 TOTAL base values over a field of size at least that,
skip discriminant zeros, factor a regular fibre and adjoin ONE residue
field of degree<=D. Test h0=1 for every supplied class by charged RR. For
rank m fixed, enumeration of ell^m classes is polynomial. Every class is
already represented over the native module's ONE common field; do not
take a growing arbitrary lcm of support fields. RR costs charge positive
and negative divisor degrees and presentations. Randomized subroutines
need capped independent restarts, not an assumed tail from expectation.

Original Frobenius/deck maps need the basepoint correction:

    D_(sigma E)^b is the unique effective member of
        |sigma(D_E^b)+g*b-g*sigma(b)|.

Replacing original Frobenius by an extension power is invalid. In char0,
a base value of height<=log(Ng³+R+1) exists; coordinate/Arakelov comparison
must still be paid. Under an ACTUAL smooth DVR model, section b and extended
line bundle E, h0=1 on the special fibre gives H1=0 and a free rank-one H0;
the canonical divisor is finite flat and specializes correctly. This is
compatibility, not an algorithm constructing those extensions.

## Exact remaining height obligation

The completed OpenAI torsion-height report correctly separates chosen small
b from arbitrary b: uniqueness alone cannot omit its height. On the fixed
elliptic curve y²=x³-2x, P=(2,2), Q=(0,0), b_N=[2^N]P gives
v2 x(b_N)=-2N and v2 x(b_N+Q)=2N+1. Unique degree-one representatives of
the fixed nonzero2-torsion class have unbounded coefficient heights. This
illustrates the missing basepoint charge; ell2 is not an odd-ell surface
counterfamily. The zero class D_0=g*b already forces the same charge at
every ell. This does NOT refute a controlled choice of small b.

Source TheoremB.4's constants are not polynomial in growing g: its displayed
comparison has4^g factors and its Jacobian representation can have exponential
size. Its use alone therefore remains insufficient. Fixed-rank GALOIS-STABLE
classes and unique divisors give polynomial individual support degrees, not
a common split-support field or automatic height bound.

The current decisive obligation is polynomial height of CLOSED torsion-divisor
encodings for a controlled b, with model height charged. An explicit source
route is under paid attack: Couveignes-Edixhoven general Chapter9 intersection
Theorems9.1.3/9.2.5, rather than a generic exponentially sized theta embedding.
Their vertical terms, support-closure hypotheses, cross-intersections and
metric integrals must be paid outside modular curves. The book's PDF text
has extraction defects; ambiguous signs require viewing the original page.
Neither a finite successful reconstruction nor canonical-height zero pays
this global bound. The six initial closure tasks plus two distinct source/
similitude follow-ups are tracked in their dispatch.json; no quantum code.

# Logarithmic-collision Merkl atlas

2026-11-12. Geometric lemma independently proved and parent-checked.
Precise proof: audits/reviews/2026-11-12-merkl-log-atlas.md. Arithmetic
transfer remains OPEN; analytic chart existence is not a BIT algorithm.
This directly targets the branch-height exponential in the surface classical
comparator, not a general-purpose geometry subsystem. Corpus query and primary
Javanpeykar1403.6404 Definition3.1.1/Theorem3.1.2 preceded this candidate.
The strongest existing bound uses a Belyi conversion with exponential dependence
on logarithmic branch height; Remark6.0.5 separately notes exponential degree
but logarithmic branch-height dependence in Bilu--Strambi. Neither is joint
polynomial. No full Faltings/coordinate-height or point-count claim follows yet.

Established geometric claim: fix r>=3. For EVERY finite holomorphic map
pi:Y->P1(C) of degree d, with Y compact connected genus>=1 and branch locus
contained in a set B of r distinct points, put delta=min pairwise chordal
separation and L=1+log(1/delta). There is a Merkl atlas for the CANONICAL
probability Arakelov measure with r1=3/4, chart count N<=C_r*d*(d+L),
c1<=C*d², and log M<=C*d. Consequently Theorem3.1.2 gives
sup gr_Y <= C_r*d³*(d+L). All constants uniform in the cover and branch positions.
No irreducibility, monodromy, real coordinates or supplied analytic charts
beyond the finite cover hypothesis are additional advice. This is a geometric
bound; implementing chart coordinates is not itself a claimed BIT algorithm.

## Proposed construction and exact risks

Use unitary Möbius coordinates on the sphere so local derivative ratios on
small spherical caps are universally controlled. For each branch point b,
choose a disjoint base disk |phi_b|<2h with h comparable to delta/100. A cover
component above that disk has a root coordinate w with phi_b(pi(w))=h*w^e,
1<=e<=d. Take the branch chart |w|<1; it extends to |w|<2^(1/e).
Its inner |w|<r1 contains all points over |phi_b|<h*r1^d.
There are at most r*d branch charts.

Cover the remaining base sphere by Whitney disks centered outside these tiny
inner holes, of radius a fixed small multiple of distance to B, capped by a
fixed spherical radius. Choose a maximal variable-radius net whose r1-inner
disks cover the complement. Their doubled disks avoid B. A dyadic packing
count gives at most C_r*(L+d) disks: at each distance scale the relevant area
is O_r(scale²), so only O_r(1) disks; the smallest required scale is comparable
to h*r1^d. Every disk lifts to d disjoint unramified charts. The lift extends
to a coordinate disk of radius at least3/2. Hence N<=C_r*d*(d+L).
CHECK the packing and coverage uniformly for clusters and hole boundaries;
no assertion based only on a picture is accepted.

Canonical density: write each globally L2-orthonormal holomorphic differential
in any enlarged chart. Mean-value bounds on a disk of radius R-1 around a
point of the unit chart give |f_nu|²<=C/(R-1)². Summing g such bounds and
normalizing the canonical measure by g cancels g. Unramified charts give
constant c1. Branch charts have R-1=2^(1/e)-1>=c/e, so c1<=C*d² on the
ENTIRE unit disk, not only its smaller inner disk. The larger branch disk is
essential; ordinary Bergman bounds on only the unit disk blow up at its boundary.

Transitions: overlapping unramified Whitney disks have comparable radii and
bounded unitary-Möbius factors, so derivatives and reciprocals are bounded.
Distinct branch disks/preimages do not overlap. On a branch/Whitney overlap,
the base Whitney radius is comparable to |phi_b|=h|w|^e. Thus derivative of
the normalized base coordinate with respect to w is comparable to e/|w|,
and its inverse to |w|/e. All Whitney centers lie outside |phi_b|<h*r1^d;
their small relative radius gives |w|>=c*r1^(d/e)>=c*r1^d throughout an
overlap. Hence M<=C*d*r1^(-d), and logM<=C*d. M itself need not be polynomial:
Merkl charges logM. CHECK transitions on ALL overlaps, not just inner overlaps.

These give precisely the four hypotheses of the actual Merkl definition,
with fixed r1>1/2. If any extension, density, overlap or counting assertion
fails, exhibit the offending finite cover/degeneration and correct the bound.
No finite numerical scan can establish this uniform claim.

## Arithmetic use stays separate

For algebraic B with bounded total Galois orbit, averaged log chordal collision
is bounded by C_r*(1+h_B) via projective height/product-formula inequalities.
Thus the proposed analytic bound would avoid exponential h_B in this Green
quantity. It does NOT alone prove stable Faltings height, finite-place
intersection estimates, bounded supplied-coordinate divisor heights, or
uniform CRT reconstruction. The known twist family y²=a*x(x-1)(x-2) still
forces charging model height. A separate source-proof audit identifies exactly
which steps of the source can use this bound and what remains. No quantum
algorithm, speedup, novelty or full classical matching is asserted.

## Final geometric disposition

The independent proof uses angular a(s)=min(1/4,dist(s,B)), radii a(s)/100,
centers outside holes theta0=(delta/100)*(3/4)^d and separation at least
min(rho_s,rho_t)/4. Balls of radius rho_s/16 are disjoint. Each distance
layer lies in r caps of proportional area; hence O_r(1) centers per layer
and O(L+d) layers. Inner coverage follows from maximality, including hole
boundaries. On a branch/Whitney overlap the center distance t<3h makes the
branch uniquely nearest; h|w|^e>=(49/100)h(3/4)^d. Both full-overlap
derivatives are bounded by M=500d(4/3)^d, while the enlarged embedded
disks give full-unit density c1<=d². This establishes all actual Merkl
hypotheses without delicate decimal constants or spectral assumptions.

The primary theorem AND appendix were checked. Its local two-sided
regularization bound is also available in these coordinates; globally only
sup gr is bounded, since gr diverges at the diagonal. The fixed-radius
asymptotic follows from the appendix before its final numerical optimization.

Completed Fable proof estimateUSD2.168550 is substantively correct; replace
its compressed nearest-branch step by the direct distance proof above. Its
reference to the separate false surface Theorem4.1 as part of this source
is rejected as a source mix-up. Opus transfer estimateUSD0.787048 is
TRUNCATED/PARTIAL, not a completed arithmetic proof. It correctly warns
that sup gr alone is insufficient; its Faltings headline is unproved here.
Six closure obligations include a new, fully sourced general-branch
arithmetic proof task. No whole surface algorithm or coordinate-height
claim follows from this geometric lemma.

## Global lower bound away from equal base images

Parent deduction independently checked: for pi(b)!=pi(x), including infinity,

    gr_Y(b,x) >= log dist_ch(pi(b),pi(x))-log(C*d)-C_r*d³*(d+L).

Apply actual Merkl on the SAME atlas with inner radius7/8; coverage and the
other hypotheses persist, with the same asymptotic local bound. Choose b
in a3/4-inner chart. Its centered circle of coordinate radius1/8 lies strictly
in the7/8-inner disk, where gr>=-log8-Lambda'. Outside that disk the source
Green function is superharmonic, so the boundary minimum principle gives
the same lower bound. Inside, the coordinate straight segment remains in
the unit disk; the spherical derivative of pi is <=C*d on branch charts
and <=C on Whitney charts. Thus coordinate distance >=dist_ch(pi b,pi x)/(Cd),
and the local regularization bound proves the claim. No global bound on
absolute gr near the diagonal, or arithmetic model conclusion, is inferred.

Uniform stable Faltings transfer is now established separately in
SURFACE_UNIFORM_ARITHMETIC_HEIGHT.md and its source-checked review. It uses
the FULL atlas rather than sup gr alone; torsion coordinate heights remain open.

# Book Theorem 9.2.5: model-minimality guard

2026-11-12. Focused source check for the parent support-height work.
Source: `../sources/surface_module_2026/couveignes_edixhoven_book.pdf`,
printed pages 195-200, PDF pages 207-212. The relevant text is Section
9.2, beginning at physical newline-based line 9347 in the retained text.
No Git, network, API, paid-context edit, or full height-chain inference.
Commands used `/opt/anaconda3/bin/python` and newline-based line counting.

## Finding

Relative minimality is NOT stated explicitly in the local opening
hypotheses of Section 9.2. They say that `X -> Spec O_K` is a
"regular, split semistable curve", with positive-genus geometrically
irreducible generic fibre. However, the written proof of Theorem 9.2.5
uses properties of the relatively minimal semistable regular model.
A regular model which is merely reduced and nodal, in Javanpeykar's
broader semistability convention, cannot be substituted without a
separate repair or contraction argument.

Two places make this necessary:

1. Theorem 9.2.5, printed pages 199-200 / PDF pages 211-212, is deduced
   from the identity in Theorem 9.2.1 by discarding a term using
   `(omega_X/B,omega_X/B)>=0` (physical lines 9561-9563).
2. The proof of Lemma 9.2.6, printed page 200 / PDF page 212, says that
   `omega_X/B`, `D`, and `D_x` intersect EVERY fibre component
   nonnegatively (physical lines 9586-9587). Relative nefness of the
   dualizing sheaf excludes rational exceptional tails.

The PDF's Theorem 9.2.5 contains the term

```
-(1/2)*(D,D-omega_X/B),
```

with the MINUS sign. The text extraction loses that sign; this review
does not use the positive-sign transcription.

The book's global convention also points toward an implicit minimal
model: Chapter 4, printed page 92 / PDF page 104, says that after finite
base extension a positive-genus curve has a UNIQUE semistable arithmetic
surface (physical lines 4490-4498). Such uniqueness is false if arbitrary
smooth-point blowups of a nodal model are admitted. Either the book's
word "semistable" includes exclusion of rational tails, or minimality is
implicit in this discussion. The source does not justify interpreting
Section 9.2 as allowing arbitrary nonminimal nodal models.

## Decisive check on a nonminimal model

Let `X_min/O_K` be a split semistable minimal regular genus-one model,
and blow up a smooth rational point of one special fibre over `s`:

```
f:X' -> X_min,       exceptional curve E.
```

The resulting surface is still regular; its fibre is reduced with an
ordinary node between `E` and the strict transform. Thus it is
semistable in Javanpeykar Definition 2.2.1's nodal sense. Javanpeykar
Remark 2.2.2 explicitly recognizes this nonminimal example.
The standard blowup and adjunction formulas give

```
omega_X'/B = f^*omega_X_min/B + E,
(E,E) = -log #k(s),
(f^*omega_X_min/B,E)=0,
(omega_X'/B,E) = -log #k(s) < 0,
(omega_X'/B,omega_X'/B)
  = (omega_X_min/B,omega_X_min/B)-log #k(s)
  = -log #k(s) < 0.
```

The last equality uses the minimal semistable genus-one canonical
self-intersection, which is zero. This refutes both properties used
by the written proof when applied to arbitrary nonminimal nodal models.
It is NOT a counterexample to the final numerical inequality of
Theorem 9.2.5: the other terms also change under blowup, and a separate
extension of that inequality could still hold.

## Consequence for the parent construction

Javanpeykar Theorem 4.3.2 supplies the MINIMAL RESOLUTION OF THE
NORMALIZATION of the finite cover. This is minimal among resolutions
of that normal surface; it need not be the RELATIVELY MINIMAL regular
model of its generic curve. Nonexceptional rational tails may remain.
The two different minimality statements must not be conflated.

Before invoking the book's written proof, either:

* pass to the relatively minimal semistable regular model and account
  explicitly for the change in the closures/intersections of `D`,
  `D_x`, and `P` under the contractions; or
* prove a nonminimal version, retaining and controlling the relevant
  canonical/exceptional contributions rather than assuming them
  nonnegative.

The exact identity in Theorem 9.2.1 may be useful for such a repair.
For instance, a smooth-point blowup decreases `omega^2` and increases
the weighted node count by the same `log #k(s)`, so their sum is
unchanged. That observation alone does not repair Lemma 9.2.6's
componentwise-nefness step. No nonminimal extension or full support-
height bound is established in this note.
